import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def discrete_log_naive_precond (g h p : UInt64) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  p.toNat > 1
  -- !benchmark @end precond

def is_discrete_log (g h p : Nat) (x : Nat) : Prop :=
  (Nat.pow g x) % p = h % p

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Linear search: returns the first index `j` in `[i, i+k)` with `f j = true`. -/
def dlSearch (f : Nat → Bool) (i : Nat) : Nat → Option Nat
  | 0 => none
  | k + 1 => if f i then some i else dlSearch f (i + 1) k

/-- The test performed at each step: `g^x % p == h % p`. -/
def dlTest (g h p : UInt64) : Nat → Bool :=
  fun x => (Nat.pow g.toNat x % p.toNat == h.toNat % p.toNat)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def discrete_log_naive (g h p : UInt64) (h_precond : discrete_log_naive_precond g h p) : Option UInt64 :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  (dlSearch (dlTest g h p) 0 p.toNat).map (fun x => UInt64.ofNat x)
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def discrete_log_naive_postcond (g h p : UInt64) (result : Option UInt64) (h_precond : discrete_log_naive_precond g h p) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  match result with
  | some x => is_discrete_log g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat x.toNat ∧ x.toNat < p.toNat ∧
               ∀ k : Nat, k < x.toNat → ¬ is_discrete_log g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat k
  | none => ∀ k : Nat, k < p.toNat → ¬ is_discrete_log g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat k
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem dlSearch_some (f : Nat → Bool) :
    ∀ (k i x : Nat), dlSearch f i k = some x →
      f x = true ∧ i ≤ x ∧ x < i + k ∧ ∀ j, i ≤ j → j < x → f j = false := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro i x hh
    simp [dlSearch] at hh
  | succ k ih =>
    intro i x hh
    by_cases hfi : f i = true
    · simp [dlSearch, hfi] at hh
      subst hh
      refine ⟨hfi, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
      intro j hj1 hj2
      exfalso
      omega
    · simp [dlSearch, hfi] at hh
      obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4⟩ := ih (i + 1) x hh
      refine ⟨h1, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
      intro j hj1 hj2
      rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le hj1 with heq | hlt
      · subst heq
        simpa using hfi
      · exact h4 j (by omega) hj2

theorem dlSearch_none (f : Nat → Bool) :
    ∀ (k i : Nat), dlSearch f i k = none → ∀ j, i ≤ j → j < i + k → f j = false := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro i _ j hj1 hj2
    exfalso
    omega
  | succ k ih =>
    intro i hnone
    by_cases hfi : f i = true
    · simp [dlSearch, hfi] at hnone
    · simp [dlSearch, hfi] at hnone
      intro j hj1 hj2
      rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le hj1 with heq | hlt
      · subst heq
        simpa using hfi
      · exact ih (i + 1) hnone j (by omega) (by omega)
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem discrete_log_naive_postcond_satisfied (g h p : UInt64) (h_precond : discrete_log_naive_precond g h p) :
    discrete_log_naive_postcond g h p (discrete_log_naive g h p h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  have hpsize : p.toNat < 18446744073709551616 := by
    first
      | exact p.toBitVec.isLt
      | exact p.val.isLt
      | exact p.toFin.isLt
      | exact UInt64.toNat_lt p
      | exact UInt64.toNat_lt_size p
      | simpa [UInt64.size] using UInt64.toNat_lt p
      | simpa [UInt64.size] using UInt64.toNat_lt_size p
      | simp
  have hdef : discrete_log_naive g h p h_precond
      = (dlSearch (dlTest g h p) 0 p.toNat).map (fun x => UInt64.ofNat x) := rfl
  rw [hdef]
  cases hs : dlSearch (dlTest g h p) 0 p.toNat with
  | none =>
    show ∀ k : Nat, k < p.toNat → ¬ is_discrete_log g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat k
    intro k hk hcon
    have hf := dlSearch_none (dlTest g h p) p.toNat 0 hs k (Nat.zero_le _) (by omega)
    have he : Nat.pow g.toNat k % p.toNat = h.toNat % p.toNat := hcon
    have hb : (Nat.pow g.toNat k % p.toNat == h.toNat % p.toNat) = false := hf
    rw [he] at hb
    simp at hb
  | some x =>
    obtain ⟨h1, _, h3, h4⟩ := dlSearch_some (dlTest g h p) p.toNat 0 x hs
    have hxlt : x < p.toNat := by omega
    have hx64 : x < 18446744073709551616 := by omega
    have hxe : (UInt64.ofNat x).toNat = x := by
      first
        | exact UInt64.toNat_ofNat_of_lt hx64
        | simp [UInt64.toNat_ofNat, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hx64]
        | simp [UInt64.toNat_ofNat, UInt64.size, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hx64]
        | simp [UInt64.toNat, UInt64.ofNat, BitVec.toNat_ofNat, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hx64]
        | (rw [UInt64.toNat_ofNat]; omega)
        | (simp [UInt64.toNat_ofNat, UInt64.size]; omega)
        | omega
    show is_discrete_log g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat (UInt64.ofNat x).toNat ∧
        (UInt64.ofNat x).toNat < p.toNat ∧
        ∀ k : Nat, k < (UInt64.ofNat x).toNat → ¬ is_discrete_log g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat k
    rw [hxe]
    refine ⟨?_, hxlt, ?_⟩
    · have h1' : (Nat.pow g.toNat x % p.toNat == h.toNat % p.toNat) = true := h1
      show Nat.pow g.toNat x % p.toNat = h.toNat % p.toNat
      first
        | exact eq_of_beq h1'
        | exact Nat.eq_of_beq_eq_true h1'
        | simpa using h1'
    · intro k hk hcon
      have hf := h4 k (Nat.zero_le _) hk
      have he : Nat.pow g.toNat k % p.toNat = h.toNat % p.toNat := hcon
      have hb : (Nat.pow g.toNat k % p.toNat == h.toNat % p.toNat) = false := hf
      rw [he] at hb
      simp at hb
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## Analysis of the error

The failure was only in the two "contradiction" spots. After `simp [dlTest] at hf`, `simp` normalized `Nat.pow g.toNat k` into `g.toNat ^ k`, so `hf : ¬ g.toNat ^ k % p.toNat = h.toNat % p.toNat` no longer syntactically matched `he : g.toNat.pow k % p.toNat = h.toNat % p.toNat`, hence `simp` couldn't use `he` and the goal `False` stayed open.

**Fix:** don't let `simp` normalize first. Instead, transfer `hf : dlTest g h p k = false` to its unfolded `beq` form by definitional equality, rewrite it with `he` (which is in the same `Nat.pow` form), and then let `simp` derive `False` from `(a == a) = false`.

## Analysis

**Implementation idea.** The cleanest verifiable formulation of the naive linear search is a helper

```
dlSearch f i k = first index j in [i, i+k) with f j = true, else none
```

defined by structural recursion on the counter `k`. With
`f x := (g^x % p == h % p)` and starting at `i = 0`, `k = p.toNat`, this exactly performs the naive search from `0` upwards, so minimality is automatic.

**Key lemmas.**
* `dlSearch_some`: if the search returns `some x`, then `f x = true`, `i ≤ x < i + k`, and every `j` with `i ≤ j < x` satisfies `f j = false` (this gives correctness *and* minimality).
* `dlSearch_none`: if it returns `none`, every `j ∈ [i, i+k)` satisfies `f j = false` (this gives the negative case).

Both are proved by induction on `k`, generalizing `i`.

**Converting `Nat → UInt64`.** The found index satisfies `x < p.toNat < 2^64`, so `(UInt64.ofNat x).toNat = x`. I derive `p.toNat < 2^64` and the `ofNat`/`toNat` roundtrip with a `first`-combinator over the various available core lemma forms (to be robust to naming across versions).

Then a `show` (definitional unfolding of the reducible postcondition and of `Option.map`) reduces the goal to the concrete conjunction / universal statement, which follows from the two lemmas (using `eq_of_beq` and a `simp` contradiction for the boolean test).
